An exact polynomial-remainder identity reduces it to the claimed rational expression; nodal convexity and mesh symmetries yield the global operator norm; a sign witness establishes sharpness. Periodic Gram inverses are periodizations of infinite inverses and give a ≤ envelope with convergence from exponentially decaying tails. Exact rational calculations for several ratios and periods and a symbolic remainder test replayed successfully; finite experiments are not substituted for infinite proof.

value.rationale: A classical spline approximation stability problem gains a sharp analytic two-parameter value, not just existence of a uniform bound. The result quantifies loss of sup-norm amplification as mesh alternation becomes asymmetric and supplies the best possible constant for a full family of finite-period spaces, providing an exact benchmarking and mesh-contrast law. The rational expression and nontrivial periodization bound are mathematically motivated by periodic knot design, unlike an arbitrary finite enumeration.
